newsitem.title: USA: Albright -- food could be US foreign policy weapon.
newsitem.headline: Albright -- food could be US foreign policy weapon.

text.p: Secretary of State-designate Madeleine Albright has said U.S. food products might be used as a weapon of U.S. foreign policy but "only in the most compelling circumstances."

In answers to more than 200 written questions posed by the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, she stressed that the Clinton adminstration is "committed to promoting the export of America's agricultural commodities."

But she acknowledged: "There may be circumstances, however, when an external threat is so central to our national interests that it is necessary to impose sanctions, including sanctions involving agricultural commodities."
"We would not seek to impose sanctions affecting the exports of agricultural products except under the most compelling circumstances," she said.

Albright said the 1996 farm bill "addresses these concerns." The law provides that unless other agricultural exporting countries join the United States in an embargo, the loss of farm income to U.S. producers must be made up by the government through direct payments to producers or enhanced support for export market development, she said.
The Senate Foreign Relations Committee Monday voted to approve Albright's nomination by President Clinton to be the first woman secretary of state. The full Senate is expected to act on Wednesday.
